title.en: A historical drawing of a Marshallese chart
title.zh: 马绍尔海图的历史绘图

alt.en: Ink lines form a roughly rectangular lattice with curved and diagonal strands, on a sheet labelled as a Marshall Islands stick chart.
alt.zh: 纸上墨线组成近矩形网格，含曲线与斜线；下方文字标明为马绍尔群岛棒图。

caption.en: Ethel Richardson, Illustration of stick chart, Marshall Islands, c.1920. Ink and graphite on paper; Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa, MU000049/008/0003.
caption.zh: 埃塞尔·理查森，《马绍尔群岛棒图插图》，约1920年，纸本墨水与石墨；新西兰蒂帕帕国家博物馆，MU000049/008/0003。

interpretation.en: This archival drawing records a Marshallese chart’s visible structure. Navigators studied charts ashore and read swells at sea. Richardson’s ink-and-graphite image is a historical depiction, not the navigational object itself.
interpretation.zh: 这张档案绘图记录马绍尔棒图的可见结构。航海者在岸上学习棒图，在海上辨读涌浪。理查森的墨水与石墨绘图是历史描绘，而非航海器物本体。

before.en:
A Marshallese navigation chart can look unlike a paper map. Curved sticks and shells bring relationships among swells and islands into a form that a learner can study. Navigators memorized such charts on land; the objects were not simply carried aboard as route maps.

The Library of Congress holds three examples made in Majuro during the 1920s. A mattang teaches wave–island relationships, while rebbelib and meddo charts show broader or more limited island groups. They should not be read as scale drawings or interchangeable keys to every Pacific navigation tradition.

This is living knowledge as well as museum history. Waan Aelõñ in Majel documents Marshallese teaching through canoe work and navigation, including Captain Joel Korent using charts with learners. The making date of an object is not the beginning or end of the knowledge it helps transmit.
before.zh:
马绍尔群岛的航海图，可能完全不像纸上的地图。弯曲枝条与贝壳，将涌浪和岛屿之间的关系变成可以学习的形式。航海者在陆上记忆这类图表，而不是简单地把它们带上船当作航线图。

美国国会图书馆保存三件1920年代在马朱罗制作的例子。mattang用于教学，呈现波浪与岛屿的关系；rebbelib和meddo则描绘较广或较小的岛群范围。它们不应被当作按比例绘制的图，也不能用来概括所有太平洋航海传统。

这既是馆藏历史，也是活态知识。Waan Aelõñ in Majel记录了通过独木舟制作与航海开展的马绍尔教学，其中包括船长Joel Korent用图表指导学员。文物的制作年代，并不代表它所传授知识的起点或终点。

after.en:
A Marshallese navigation chart can look unlike a paper map. Curved sticks and shells bring relationships among swells and islands into a form that a learner can study. Navigators memorized such charts on land; the objects were not simply carried aboard as route maps.

The Library of Congress holds three examples made in Majuro during the 1920s. A mattang teaches wave–island relationships, while rebbelib and meddo charts show broader or more limited island groups. They should not be read as scale drawings or interchangeable keys to every Pacific navigation tradition.

This is living knowledge as well as museum history. Waan Aelõñ in Majel documents Marshallese teaching through canoe work and navigation, including Captain Joel Korent using charts with learners. The making date of an object is not the beginning or end of the knowledge it helps transmit.

A drawing made around 1920 by Ethel Richardson, now in Te Papa’s museum archive, records a Marshall Islands stick chart in ink and graphite. Its lattice of straight and curved lines preserves an outsider’s graphic record of the object. The drawing complements, rather than replaces, Marshallese teaching about how swells meet islands.
after.zh:
马绍尔群岛的航海图，可能完全不像纸上的地图。弯曲枝条与贝壳，将涌浪和岛屿之间的关系变成可以学习的形式。航海者在陆上记忆这类图表，而不是简单地把它们带上船当作航线图。

美国国会图书馆保存三件1920年代在马朱罗制作的例子。mattang用于教学，呈现波浪与岛屿的关系；rebbelib和meddo则描绘较广或较小的岛群范围。它们不应被当作按比例绘制的图，也不能用来概括所有太平洋航海传统。

这既是馆藏历史，也是活态知识。Waan Aelõñ in Majel记录了通过独木舟制作与航海开展的马绍尔教学，其中包括船长Joel Korent用图表指导学员。文物的制作年代，并不代表它所传授知识的起点或终点。

蒂帕帕博物馆档案保存埃塞尔·理查森约1920年以墨水与石墨绘制的马绍尔群岛棒图。直线与曲线交织的网格留下外来绘图者对该物件的图像记录。它可与马绍尔人关于涌浪和岛屿关系的教学相互参照，却不能取代这种知识传授。
